Meanwhile, a cache keeps hot rows near the application, so repeated reads skip the slow trip to disk. Every hit saves time and shields the primary database; every miss, though, still pays full price, and a bigger cache may help.

However, speed has a cost, because stale entries can mislead users. Teams therefore set expiry timers, invalidate keys after writes, and choose eviction policies such as least recently used; each choice trades freshness against hit rate. A cold cache also needs warming, or the very first requests will stampede the database before the cache recovers.

Along this path, a quick lookup in main RAM can lift a slow disk from strain; but old data is a trap, so a smart tool must drop, patch, or void any old copy right as a row shifts.

Finally, measure your cache hit ratio, tune lifetimes with real traffic, and keep correctness first until the work is done.
